=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Package

**Preliminary note:** The Seller's cover note asks us to skip every [STANDARD] item and says the limitation package is "FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened." Those labels don't bind Wattlebridge. The Buyer hasn't agreed to them, so I've reviewed all 16 items. The Seller's market-practice figures (10-20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12-18 month survival) are unsupported assertions. Test them against comparable deal data before accepting them.

**Known quantified exposures:** Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 0.42m, Ironquay AUD 0.18m, and Sandbar AUD 0.33m total about AUD 4.13m. The Bluefen revenue (~AUD 3.6m) affects value, and the export incident is unquantified. Several of these are price or debt-like items under the debt-free/cash-free mechanism, not warranty claims. They should be dealt with in the price and funds flow, so they don't consume the general cap.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller position:** Aggregate general warranty liability capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap (25-30%, or 100% of price for fundamental items). Known issues handled through specific indemnities or price adjustments, outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30%, with known issues carved out. *Reason: a 20% cap is already consumed by known exposures if they are routed through warranty claims.*

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket (~1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** Lower de minimis (around AUD 10,000, with related claims aggregated) and a "tipping" basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded), or a basket of around 0.5% of price (~AUD 120,000).
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a tipping basket at 0.5%. *Reason: a deductible basket of this size means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of any warranty loss.*

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller position:** 18 months for general warranties, applied to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 24-36 months for general warranties, longer for tax, and a limitation period that applies only to the claim category it governs.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months general, tax until 60 days after the ATO time-bar date. *Reason: 18 months may expire before known issues (lease, privacy, Ironquay) fully surface or are assessed.*

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Title and capacity capped at 100% of price, outside the basket and de minimis, with survival of at least 6 years (matching the NSW contract limitation period).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: title is the core asset being bought, and capping it at AUD 4.8m with 18-month survival leaves the Buyer exposed on the thing it is paying for.*

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** Not expressly addressed. The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5), which would catch fraud claims on their face.
- **Buyer wants:** An express clause that nothing in the SPA limits liability for fraud, including fraud by the Seller or Company officers, and that the carve-out overrides the cap, basket, time limits and non-reliance clause.
- **Recommendation:** Require an express carve-out. *Reason: the wording as drafted purports to exclude fraud, and an express carve-out removes the argument; NSW counsel should confirm the enforceability position.*

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room (to 5.00pm 22 Sept 2026) and all public registers, without limiting specific disclosure (DL 1.1-1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only of specific matters, fairly disclosed with reasonable particularity. Data room contents and public records are not disclosed against the warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. *Reason: a data room dump would disclose almost anything and gut the warranty package.*

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller position:** No Buyer claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** A pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's knowledge does not prejudice warranty or indemnity claims, and specific indemnities are unaffected by knowledge. Disclosure against warranties is limited to fair specific disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; counter with an express pro-sandbagging clause. *Reason: the Buyer's diligence is what identified these issues, and the Seller would otherwise use that diligence to defeat claims.*

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller position:** Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent; Seller to use reasonable endeavours. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue. No final consent in the data room; conditions in cl 11.3 unsatisfied (DL 2).
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen written consent as a condition precedent to Completion, unconditional or on terms acceptable to the Buyer, with a walk-away right. If waived, a price adjustment or specific indemnity for lost revenue.
- **Recommendation:** Make consent a CP. *Reason: losing a 30% revenue customer on change of control is a value-level risk that a warranty cannot cure.*

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller position:** AUD 3.2m facility to be released "following Completion." Facility not repaid; no discharge of security (DL 3).
- **Buyer wants:** Payout at Completion from the purchase price (treated as debt under the debt-free mechanism), with a payout letter and release of all security, including PPSR registrations. Confirm whether Riverlark holds security over the shares (see SPA-N-015).
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. *Reason: the Buyer would take a company subject to a AUD 3.2m secured debt with no security release, which breaches the debt-free basis.*

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller position:** Bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not in the funds flow. Payroll tax and on-costs not addressed (DL 5).
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses (including payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs) treated as Seller-borne debt-like items, deducted from price or paid by the Seller through the funds flow.
- **Recommendation:** Require inclusion in the funds flow as a deduction. *Reason: under a debt-free/cash-free deal, unpaid completion-linked liabilities belong to the Seller.*

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, described as "adequate." AUD 180,000 open; transfer of project materials conditional on full payment (cl 7.3); no receipt or confirmatory assignment (DL 4).
- **Buyer wants:** Payment of the AUD 180,000 before Completion (or deduction from price), a confirmatory assignment of all Ironquay IP, and a specific IP-title indemnity covering claims from Ironquay or related parties, outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "adequate." *Reason: the Company may not own the SOW3 IP until payment, and a payment-only indemnity doesn't cover ownership claims.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" (cl 4.6 / Sch 6). Investigation ongoing. Export may include ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). Unauthorised access and notification obligations unresolved (DL 6).
- **Buyer wants:** Completion of forensic investigation before signing or Completion; a specific indemnity for all losses from the incident (including notification, regulator, and third-party claims) outside the general cap and basket; Seller control of response costs; and a retention or escrow sized to the exposure.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus retention. *Reason: personal information was exposed to an unintended external address, and the Company may have Notifiable Data Breach Scheme obligations under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). The Seller's "not material" view is unsupported by the disclosure.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued, or ordinary course (DL 8).
- **Buyer wants:** Copies of all three contracts, confirmation of term and termination rights, and allocation of pre-Completion costs to the Seller. Any prepaid or accrued amounts treated as working capital or debt-like. Check whether the three renewals were split to avoid a threshold.
- **Recommendation:** Obtain contracts; allocate pre-Completion costs to Seller. *Reason: "ordinary course" is a characterisation, not evidence, and the renewals may bind the Company beyond Completion.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** A single general regime applies to all claims (general, title, tax, IP, specific).
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for: general warranties; fundamental/title and capacity; tax (uncapped to price, longer survival); IP; specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, lease/consent if applicable); and fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject single regime; require separate categories. *Reason: a single cap and time limit for all claim types means the highest-risk items get the lowest protection.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title to 100% of shares evidenced by the share register at DD-012 showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder (DL 10). The disclosure does not state that the Buyer has verified this itself.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: current ASIC company extract, inspection of the original register, PPSR and security searches (including any Riverlark security over shares), confirmation of no pending transfers, and delivery of executed share transfer forms at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Run independent verification before signing. *Reason: the register is a seller-prepared document, and title is the core asset.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (no specific terms).
- **Buyer wants:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity (uncapped to price, surviving to 60 days after ATO time bar), and IP warranties (ownership, non-infringement, no open-source contamination, and the Ironquay position) with longer survival and outside the basket.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: tax and IP are open items with no agreed terms, and applying the general regime to them is not acceptable.*

---

**Priority for the Buyer's mark-up:** (1) Riverlark payout and debt treatment; (2) Bluefen CP; (3) fraud carve-out and reject the general disclosure, buyer-knowledge and single-regime positions; (4) fundamental/title regime; (5) specific indemnities for Ironquay and the privacy incident; (6) the funds flow for bonuses and Sandbar; (7) general cap, basket and time limits.

*This is a preliminary review of the Seller's documents. NSW counsel should confirm enforceability (including the fraud position), the Privacy Act obligations, the lease and Mossvale consent analysis (DL 7, 9), and the tax survival periods before the mark-up goes out.*
